text:
alex_m: Heads up — after the normalization deploy a bunch of users are showing up in multiple groups. Support ticket with a few samples.

sana: can you paste one of the affected user payloads?

alex_m: here's a scrubbed example we got from the webhook:
```json
{
  "userName": "taylor@example.com",
  "id": "12345",
  "externalId": "EMP-987",
  "memberships": [ { "groupId": "eng-team", "membership_canonical_id": "ENG:12345" } ]
}
```

jordan: :eyes: looks like `membership_canonical_id` changed shape after the attr normalization. Our old canonicalization used `employeeId` with zero-pad, new pipeline uses `externalId` without pad. That means the reconcile job sees them as distinct and readds members.

kevin: that would explain transient admin access in a few tenants — group A and group A-legacy both exist but map differently. Any deploy logs?

deploy-bot: deploy 2024-11-10T14:02Z applied to `scim-normalizer` (rev b3f7).

maria: quick question — did we rotate the KMS key used for membership signing last week? If signatures changed, our id canonicalizer might fail to dedupe.

jordan: no KMS rotation for that key. This is purely format/attr change. I pulled the mapping config:
```yaml
scim_mapping:
  canonical_id: "{{ if user.externalId }}{{ user.externalId }}{{ else }}{{ user.employeeId | pad(6) }}{{ end }}"
```

alex_m: old normalize job used pad, new one omitted pad. Ops forgot to keep the fallback.

sana: remediation options? rollback? hotfix mapping?

kevin: safest is to patch `scim-normalizer` to reintroduce the padded fallback and run a one-off reconcile to clean duplicate memberships. Also run a backfill to canonicalize `membership_canonical_id` for last 7 days of deltas.

maria: We should also add an audit alert for membership churn > X% for a tenant in 10m window. This drift caused privilege surface area to expand briefly. Need audit log entries for every membership add/remove (who triggered, source).

jordan: Agreed. I'll open a PR for the mapping fix and add a migration script: `scripts/reconcile_memberships --from 2024-11-03 --to now --canonicalize`. The script will: 1) compute canonical id per patched logic, 2) dedupe group membership events, 3) emit `audit.membership.review` events.

alex_m: timeline? support wants a mitigation before EOD PST.

jordan: patch & deploy to staging in 30m, run reconcile in staging, if green deploy to prod + run reconcile with rate limit.

kevin: while doing this, we should lock down any canary RBAC policies that let service accounts grant high privileges via group membership. Also add temporary manual approval for group changes for 2 hours post-deploy.

maria: I'll file a compliance ticket so we have evidence of the change and the remediation steps (including the audit events and the backfill output).

sana: any edgecases where users will get removed permanently? we have to avoid accidental deprovisioning of guests.

jordan: reconcile will prefer add+dedupe, not blind delete. We'll only remove memberships where there's authoritative tombstone from SCIM provider.

alex_m: thanks. I'll update the support ticket and notify affected customers. :thumbsup:

maria: postmortem and follow-ups: add a pre-deploy checklist item for any normalization logic that changes canonical IDs, and add a unit test for `canonical_id` variance.

kevin: +1. Also file an infra alert if `membership_canonical_id` hash distribution changes >10% day-over-day.

jordan: PR link sent: https://git.redwood.ai/r/scim-normalizer/pulls/42 (WIP).

alex_m: great. ping me when prod reconcile starts.

sana: thanks everyone, will monitor support queue. :mag:
